title: Impair Defenses
summary: Impairing defenses is the deliberate degradation, misconfiguration or removal of security controls so that subsequent activity is neither observed nor blocked. The mechanism exploits the fact that defenders administer their own tools through the same operating system, directory and cloud control planes the adversary is trying to reach. On endpoints this can mean stopping or disabling antivirus and endpoint detection services, altering their configuration to add exclusions, unloading security drivers, tampering with logging agents, or editing firewall rules to permit traffic that policy would otherwise deny. In the identity and cloud control plane it can mean weakening audit configuration, disabling conditional access or log export, removing alerting integrations, or using a legitimate administrative role to change a policy that protects many accounts at once. A quieter variant disables nothing outright but blinds a specific sensor by reducing event verbosity, excluding a directory from scanning, or reconfiguring a collection rule so the activity of interest stops generating records. The artefacts are unusually valuable because they look administrative. Service state transitions, configuration and registry changes to security products, termination of protected processes, audit policy modifications, unexpected gaps in log ingestion and control plane change records all appear in the same places legitimate administration appears. Investigators therefore treat timing, actor and authorisation as the discriminators. A change made during a maintenance window by a known engineering account, with a change record and a plausible scope, is routine. The same change made outside any window by a newly created or compromised account, scoped narrowly to the hosts or accounts currently under investigation, and immediately followed by unusual authentication or execution activity, is a strong indicator. Gaps in telemetry matter as much as explicit disablement: a host that stops reporting, a sensor that no longer emits an expected event class, or a retention setting quietly shortened can serve the same objective with far less noise.
objectives: Explain how endpoint, directory and cloud control planes can each be used to degrade or disable security controls.
Recognise the administrative looking artefacts that indicate tampering, including service state changes and security product configuration edits.
Use telemetry gaps and unexpected changes in log volume as evidence in their own right.
Differentiate sanctioned maintenance from malicious impairment using change records, actor identity, scope and timing.
Correlate impairment events with the authentication, discovery or execution activity that follows them.
Recommend monitoring and hardening that keeps tamper attempts visible even when a control has been successfully disabled.
